title: Reading & Comprehension
description: Learn English sounds and common words, then read sentences, paragraphs, instructions and scholarship pages with confidence.

lessons.title: The Alphabet and Phonics
lessons.summary: Sounds of English letters and common combinations
lessons.content:
English has 26 letters. But it has more than 40 sounds. This is why English spelling can feel hard. Do not worry. We will learn step by step.

Vowels

Five letters are vowels: a, e, i, o, u. Every English word has at least one vowel sound.

  • a as in bag
  • e as in bed
  • i as in sit
  • o as in hot
  • u as in cup

Letter pairs

Some letters make one new sound when they are together:

  • sh as in shop
  • ch as in chair
  • th as in think and this
  • ph sounds like f, as in phone

Tip: Kinyarwanda and Swahili are read the way they are written. English is not always like that. Listen to words, then say them out loud.

quiz.question: How many letters are in the English alphabet?
quiz.explanation: English has 26 letters, but more than 40 sounds.

quiz.question: Which of these is a vowel?
quiz.explanation: The vowels are a, e, i, o and u.

quiz.question: In the word 'phone', the letters 'ph' sound like…
quiz.explanation: 'ph' makes an 'f' sound, as in phone and photo.

lessons.title: Basic Vocabulary
lessons.summary: The most common English words, with audio
lessons.content:
About 100 words make up half of everything people write in English. If you know them well, reading becomes much easier.

Words you will see everywhere

the, a, an, and, is, are, was, to, of, in, for, on, with, you, I, we, they, have, do, can, will

Words for applications

  • apply — to ask formally for something, like a place at a university
  • deadline — the last day you can do something
  • eligible — allowed to apply because you meet the rules
  • requirement — something you must have or do
  • submit — to send your finished work or form

Practice: Write each word in a notebook. Write one sentence with it. For example: The deadline is 30 March.

quiz.question: What does 'deadline' mean?
options: The last day you can do something
quiz.answer: The last day you can do something
quiz.explanation: A deadline is the final day. After it, you cannot apply.

quiz.question: If you are 'eligible', you…
quiz.explanation: Eligible means you are allowed to apply because you meet the rules.

quiz.question: Choose the correct sentence.
quiz.explanation: 'Yesterday' is in the past, so we use the past tense: submitted.

title: Introduction to Computers
description: Learn what a computer is, how to use a keyboard and mouse, and how to save and find your files.

lessons.title: What is a Computer?
lessons.summary: Desktop vs laptop vs tablet vs smartphone
lessons.content:
A computer is a machine that stores information and follows instructions. You may already use one every day: your smartphone is a small computer.

Four kinds of computers

  • Desktop — stays on a table. It has a separate screen, keyboard and mouse. It needs electricity all the time.
  • Laptop — folds closed and has a battery. You can carry it.
  • Tablet — a flat touch screen, bigger than a phone.
  • Smartphone — fits in your pocket. Good for messages, but hard for writing long documents.

Why this matters for you

Most university applications are easier on a laptop or desktop. You will type essays and upload documents. If you do not own one, a school, library, or cyber café can help.

quiz.question: Which computer usually has a battery and folds closed?
quiz.explanation: A laptop folds closed and runs on a battery, so you can carry it.

quiz.question: Is a smartphone a computer?
quiz.explanation: A smartphone is a small computer. It stores information and runs programs.

quiz.question: For writing a long scholarship essay, which is usually easiest?
quiz.explanation: A full keyboard and a bigger screen make long writing much easier.
